title: True Fasting
english: Root and foundation of the pious is fasting according to God, accomplished with reverence and holy prayers and alms.

For God does not desire abstinence from bread and water, but rather abstinence from evil deeds; 'For it is not what enters into the mouth that defiles the man, but what comes out of the mouth, those things defile the man' (Mark 7:15).

Let us fast, beloved, a fasting pleasing to God, about which the Lord says, 'But when you fast, anoint your head' (Matthew 6:17) through good works and alms, 'and wash your face' (Matthew 6:17), stripping away all the filth of sin.
There is a fasting that is reprehensible and there is a fasting that is praiseworthy. Many who fasted committed murders, and many who fasted saved others.
The Ninevites fasted and were saved, and through fasting they changed the anger of God. For the prophet says, 'Yet three days and Nineveh shall be overthrown' (Jonah 3:4).

He did not say, 'After three days Nineveh shall be overthrown'; for if he had said, 'After three days,' it would have been overthrown, but 'Yet three days,' this shows, 'So much time I have been patient with you and you did not repent. Yet three days I endure you, and if you do not repent in these three days, then the city shall be overthrown' (Jonah 3:4).
And for so much time they did not repent, except through the three days, that is, through the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
Jews fasted and took counsel to kill the Apostle Paul. Jezebel proclaimed a fast and killed Naboth and took the vineyard of the poor. What kind of fast is this?

Daniel fasted when he was thrown into the den of lions; for having been thrown into the den, he cried out to Christ, saying, 'Out of the depths I have cried to you, Lord; Lord, hear my prayer' (Psalm 130:1).

Seeing the lions on his right and on his left, he cried out again, saying, 'Do not give to the beasts the soul confessing to you' (Psalm 50:7). See that the Lord does not abandon those who hope in him.
